newsitem.title: USA: Paxson sees adding 5-10 TV stations in 97.
newsitem.headline: Paxson sees adding 5-10 TV stations in 97.

text.p: Paxson Communications Corp expects to add five to 10 television stations this year and another five to 10 stations in 1998, Seth Grossman said Wednesday.
Grossman, vice president of corporate development, addressed a Montgomery Securities conference here, which was also attended by Lowell Paxson, company chairman.
Grossman said the company hopes to reach 63 percent of total U.S. households if the company reaches its goal for this year.
Paxson owns 55 TV stations in the U.S. The company this week announced it was selling its radio holdings to Clear Channel Communications Corp for $693 million in cash.
Earlier this month it acquired television station WJUE TV-43 from William B Popjes for an undisclosed amount.
Grossman said the company's goal by the end of 1998 was to reach 70 percent of total US households.
Paxson currently runs long-form commercials, otherwise known as "infomercials" on its stations.
